audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel / Shemuel Aleph chapter 29, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Aphek/Jezreel geography, Philistine military organization, Hebrew label, Achish's defense of David, commanders' security concern, victory-song memory, YHWH oath, David's ambiguous loyalty language, and dismissal at dawn.

verses.restored: Philistines gathered all their camps at Aphek, and Israel was camping by spring that is in Jezreel.

familiar.text: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites pitched by a fountain which is in Jezreel.

modern.text: Now the Philistines brought all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.

original.text: וַיִּקְבְּצ֧וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אֶת כָּל מַחֲנֵיהֶ֖ם אֲפֵ֑קָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל חֹנִ֔ים בַּעַ֖יִן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיִזְרְעֶֽאל

verses.restored: Lords of Philistines were passing by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men were passing at rear with Achish.

familiar.text: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rereward with Achish.

modern.text: As the Philistine leaders marched out their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men marched behind them with Achish.

original.text: וְסַרְנֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ עֹֽבְרִ֔ים לְמֵא֖וֹת וְלַאֲלָפִ֑ים וְדָוִ֣ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו עֹֽבְרִ֛ים בָּאַחֲרֹנָ֖ה עִם אָכִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Commanders of Philistines said, What are these Hebrews? Achish said to commanders of Philistines, Is this not David, servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days or these years? I have found nothing against him from day of his falling away until this day.

familiar.text: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What do these Hebrews here? And Achish said unto the princes of the Philistines, Is not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, which hath been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell unto me unto this day?

modern.text: Then the commanders of the Philistines asked, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish replied, “Is this not David, the servant of King Saul of Israel? He has been with me all these days, even years, and from the day he defected until today I have found no fault in him.”

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מָ֖ה הָעִבְרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים הֲלֽוֹא זֶ֨ה דָוִ֜ד עֶ֣בֶד שָׁא֣וּל מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה אִתִּי֙ זֶ֤ה יָמִים֙ אוֹ זֶ֣ה שָׁנִ֔ים וְלֹֽא מָצָ֤אתִי בוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה מִיּ֥וֹם נָפְל֖וֹ עַד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Commanders of Philistines were angry against him. Commanders of Philistines said to him, Return the man, and let him return to his place where you appointed him. He shall not go down with us into battle, so that he does not become an adversary to us in battle. With what could this one make himself acceptable to his lord? Is it not with heads of these men?

familiar.text: And the princes of the Philistines were wroth with him; and the princes of the Philistines said unto him, Make this fellow return, that he may go again to his place which thou hast appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for wherewith should he reconcile himself unto his master? should it not be with the heads of these men?

modern.text: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with Achish and told him, “Send that man back and let him return to the place you assigned him. He must not go down with us into battle only to become our adversary during the war. What better way for him to regain the favor of his master than with the heads of our men?

original.text: וַיִּקְצְפ֨וּ עָלָ֜יו שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לוֹ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים הָשֵׁ֣ב אֶת הָאִ֗ישׁ וְיָשֹׁב֙ אֶל מְקוֹמוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִפְקַדְתּ֣וֹ שָׁ֔ם וְלֹֽא יֵרֵ֤ד עִמָּ֨נוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹא יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֥נוּ לְשָׂטָ֖ן בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וּבַמֶּ֗ה יִתְרַצֶּ֥ה זֶה֙ אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֲל֕וֹא בְּרָאשֵׁ֖י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָהֵֽם

verses.restored: Is this not David of whom they answered in dances, saying, Saul struck his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

familiar.text: Is not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

modern.text: Is this not the David about whom they sing in their dances: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”

original.text: הֲלוֹא זֶ֣ה דָוִ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יַעֲנוּ ל֛וֹ בַּמְּחֹל֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בַּֽאֲלָפָ֔יו וְדָוִ֖ד ברבבתו

verses.restored: Achish called David and said to him, As YHWH lives, you are upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in camp is good in my eyes, because I have not found evil in you from day you came to me until this day. Yet in eyes of lords you are not good.

familiar.text: Then Achish called David, and said unto him, Surely, as the LORD liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the host is good in my sight: for I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming unto me unto this day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not.

modern.text: So Achish summoned David and told him, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright in my sight, and it seems right that you should march in and out with me in the army, because I have found no fault in you from the day you came to me until this day. But you have no favor in the sight of the leaders.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל דָּוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לָיו חַי יְהוָ֞ה כִּי יָשָׁ֣ר אַתָּ֗ה וְט֣וֹב בְּ֠עֵינַי צֵאתְךָ֨ וּבֹאֲךָ֤ אִתִּי֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹֽא מָצָ֤אתִֽי בְךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם בֹּאֲךָ֥ אֵלַ֖י עַד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּבְעֵינֵ֥י הַסְּרָנִ֖ים לֹֽא ט֥וֹב אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Now return and go in peace, and do not do evil in eyes of lords of Philistines.

familiar.text: Wherefore now return, and go in peace, that thou displease not the lords of the Philistines.

modern.text: Therefore turn back now and go in peace, so that you will not do anything to displease the leaders of the Philistines.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֥ה שׁ֖וּב וְלֵ֣ךְ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וְלֹֽא תַעֲשֶׂ֣ה רָ֔ע בְּעֵינֵ֖י סַרְנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: David said to Achish, But what have I done, and what have you found in your servant from day I was before you until this day, that I may not come and fight against enemies of my lord the king?

familiar.text: And David said unto Achish, But what have I done? and what hast thou found in thy servant so long as I have been with thee unto this day, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king?

modern.text: “But what have I done?” David replied. “What have you found against your servant, from the day I came to you until today, to keep me from going along to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל אָכִ֗ישׁ כִּ֣י מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ וּמַה מָּצָ֣אתָ בְעַבְדְּךָ֔ מִיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיִ֣יתִי לְפָנֶ֔יךָ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אָבוֹא֙ וְנִלְחַ֔מְתִּי בְּאֹיְבֵ֖י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Achish answered and said to David, I know that you are good in my eyes like messenger of Divine. Nevertheless commanders of Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us into battle.

familiar.text: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou art good in my sight, as an angel of God: notwithstanding the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.

modern.text: Achish replied, “I know that you are as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God. But the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He must not go into battle with us.’

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַן אָכִישׁ֮ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל דָּוִד֒ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב אַתָּ֛ה בְּעֵינַ֖י כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ אֱלֹהִ֑ים אַ֣ךְ שָׂרֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹֽא יַעֲלֶ֥ה עִמָּ֖נוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: Now rise early in morning, you and servants of your lord who came with you. Rise early in morning, and when it is light for you, go.

familiar.text: Wherefore now rise up early in the morning with thy master’s servants that are come with thee: and as soon as ye be up early in the morning, and have light, depart.

modern.text: Now then, get up early in the morning, along with your master’s servants who came with you, and go as soon as it is light.”

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְעַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אוּ אִתָּ֑ךְ וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְא֥וֹר לָכֶ֖ם וָלֵֽכוּ

verses.restored: David rose early, he and his men, to go in morning to return to land of Philistines, and Philistines went up to Jezreel.

familiar.text: So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

modern.text: So David and his men got up early in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם דָּוִ֜ד ה֤וּא וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת בַּבֹּ֔קֶר לָשׁ֖וּב אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים עָל֥וּ יִזְרְעֶֽאל

translation_notes: Philistine commanders' distrust arises in a specific wartime coalition and from David's known history. It may not justify modern ethnic profiling, collective suspicion, or calling refugees security threats.
Achish's oath by YHWH shows religious language crossing community boundaries; it does not establish that his judgment of David is accurate.
David's words remain strategically ambiguous in context. The chapter does not reveal whether he intended to fight Israel, defect in battle, or preserve his cover.
Coalition commanders set a military boundary against Achish's patronage decision. Shared leadership can restrain a powerful sponsor, though the setting remains preparation for war.
David's exclusion protects him from immediate participation in the battle where Saul and Jonathan will die, but it does not erase his prior massacres or deception.
The phrase 'these Hebrews' belongs to ancient identity politics and must not become a modern slur or antisemitic category.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to stigmatize migrants, refugees, dual nationals, or minority soldiers as inherently disloyal. Do not portray strategic ambiguity as simple holiness. The scene is a coalition-security dispute inside an unjust war system, not a template for ethnic exclusion.
